edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase upstream of the mevalonate pathway, which lowers cholesterol synthesis and can also modestly reduce endogenous coenzyme Q10 production. That biochemical linkage explains why Coenzyme Q10 status is discussed mostly as a monitoring question rather than a severe toxicity in most users.
edges.summary: Statin therapy appears tied to adverse shifts in coenzyme q10 status in adults taking statins mainly through pooled meta-analytic evidence. This is one of the cleaner pharmacology edges in the set because the adverse pathway is predictable and monitoring can often reduce harm.
edges.caveats: Medication benefits may still outweigh this risk. The practical implication is usually monitoring, dosing separation, or targeted supplementation rather than indiscriminate discontinuation.
